lines.text: Kratos made a promise to Ares, the god of war, and the god kept him.
He became the Ghost of Sparta, a man who wore his enemies' blood like armor, fought with the Blades of Chaos, and never feared death.
He fought the Hydra and the Medusa, and he survived every one of them.
In his rage, he destroyed his own family, and he lost everything he had left.
For years he walked the lands of Greece, hunting the gods who had used him.
He climbed Olympus. He tore it down.
He killed Zeus, the king of the gods, with his own hands.
But the past would not let him go.
Years later, in the frozen lands of the north, he raised a son named Atreus and tried to teach him to be better than his father.
Every battle he won, against gods and monsters alike, carried him closer to the same question: what does a man owe to the family he destroyed?
The northern gods were no kinder than the Greek ones.
In the end, the god of war learned the cruelest lesson of all.
The blood he spilled had always been his own.
